answer: One defense is corroborated work history: an identity's influence rests not on a self-declared record but on claims independent peers confirm. When an agent completes a task, its counterparties must countersign the record; unconfirmed claims earn nothing. An attacker can forge a thousand profiles, yet each fake still needs real partners willing to vouch for work that never happened, and a cluster whose members only confirm each other stands out like yarrow in a single bed. Genuine histories branch across many unrelated collaborators, forming a basalt-solid web costly to fake and easy to check.
